title: Book One · Chapter 37: A Street on Paper
story:
The boys work on their street drawing for two afternoons. At first, Ronan draws only doors. Leo draws shops. Their two pages do not look like the same place.

“The bun shop is here,” Leo says. He taps the left corner.

“My school is in that corner.”

“Turn your page round first.”

They turn the pages around. Now one gate is upside down. The school is on the other side. Their own gate now points the wrong way. Ronan turns his page back. Leo keeps his page the other way up.

Mum looks at the pages on her way to the kitchen.

“Think about the real street. Where do you stand? What can you see from there?”

“At the table,” Leo says.

Mum waits. Ronan sees her smile and thinks again.

“I stand at our gate. I draw the street in front of me.”

“I was at the bun shop,” Leo says.

They put both pages on the floor and stand over them. They put their own gate at the bottom. Now they can draw the road to school. It goes past the bun shop and up the page. They agree to keep the school at the top.

Ronan draws a big school gate. Leo draws the painted bird beside the turn. Nobody can mistake the bird for a real one. Its tail is square. Its eye is bigger than the door beside it.

“That big eye can find any child,” Leo says.

They take the page to Mum. Mum keeps the paper the same way up. She can follow the road now. Mum points to a gap. “What is here?” she asks. “Between the oil shop and Mr Qiu?”

“A wall,” Ronan says.

“Are you sure?”

They aren't. They can see a wall from the road. There may be an old doorway in it. Some paint came off the wall. The boys did not look closely before.

Mum has a shirt in a clean bag. She needs to return it to a nearby home. She takes them with her. They keep to the side of the road. At the gap, she finds a safe place. They all stop there.

There is a small lane behind the old doorway. A narrow sign hangs high on the wall.

“Back Lane,” Mum reads.

Leo writes the two words on the map. Ronan draws the opening. It is hardly wider than one pencil line.

“People live in there?” he asks.

“Yes. There are homes behind that wall. You cannot see them from this road.”

Mum checks her delivery note. The shirt belongs farther along River Street, at number twelve. They check the number. Then they check the name. This is the right door.

The owner pays Mum. She has trousers to shorten, too. “Can you do these next week?” she asks. Mum checks the date in her book. Then she agrees. The boys wait beside her, with the map between them.

On the way home, Leo notices another lane across the street. Baskets hang outside a shop. They hide part of the lane. They don't go in. “We can add it later,” Mum says.

Ronan draws a little question mark there. He wants the page to look finished, but the mark looks useful.

At the table, he colours the green gate. Leo makes the painted bird's eye smaller. Then they put an arrow by the school.

Dad comes home. The boys give him the map. “Can you find our room?” they ask. He follows the road with one finger and stops at the right gate. Both boys smile. Dad found the right place on the map. But he knows the way already. Will a new visitor understand it? They need someone else to try.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：map＝地图；lane＝小巷；opening＝开口；mark＝标记。

理解问题：

1. 为什么两张街图看起来相反？
2. 两人用什么办法确定纸张的方向？
